How to read it

The five price fields are the same number in five costumes. Fill in whichever one you have and read off the rest.

To win is the profit on its own. Payout is that profit plus your stake back, which is the figure a book prints on the slip.

A Kalshi multiplier is the payout for every $1, so it is the same number as the decimal price. A 2.50× ticket is decimal 2.50 and +150.

Legs on the parlay tab take any of the five forms as well, one per leg.

Fees are charged on top of the bet amount and do not come back, so they come out of To win and make your true price worse. Leave the box empty if the book takes none.

Want the chance behind the price instead? The odds converter turns a percentage into a price and a price back into a percentage, and the cheat sheet lists every percent from 1 to 99. Open the odds converter →

Why five fields

Every book writes the same price differently. American books use +150 and −110. European books and most exchanges use decimals. British books use fractions. Exchanges such as Kalshi show a multiplier, which is what one dollar comes back as. They all say the same thing.

The Kalshi case

Kalshi quotes a contract in cents and shows the ticket as a multiplier: 3.33×, say. There is no American price on the screen. Put 3.33 in the multiplier field and you get +233, decimal 3.33, and 30.03%. That is the number you need to compare the ticket against a sportsbook line.

A multiplier is the whole payout, not the profit. 3.33× on $10 returns $33.30, of which $23.30 is profit.

When the legs do not multiply to the payout

On a combo ticket the leg multipliers printed on the card often do not multiply to the payout the book has committed to. They are display values, rounded or refreshed, and not always the prices the ticket was built from. The cost and the payout are the two numbers the book is bound by, so their ratio is the real price of the ticket. Divide the payout by the cost and put that in the multiplier field.

Fees

Some books, exchanges above all, take a fee on top of the stake. The fee does not come back when the bet wins, so it is a straight subtraction from the profit. Put it in the fees box and To win drops by that amount, while the payout stays as the book states it. The line under the figures then gives your true price, which is the payout over everything you paid.

Implied chance

The percentage field is the break-even rate. At +150 the bet must win 40% of the time to break even. It is the raw price with the vig still in it, so it is not a fair estimate on its own: use the devig tool for that.
